name: f1-risk-signal-v1
idea_origin: diagnostic:unanswered risk signals in F1 traces (lab/reports/cloud-run-diagnostics/block5-generation.md) + playbook:P20 base (f1-core-v1 text)
operator: refine (single fix on the subtracted core)
target_failure: Trust crisis (a second blow-up) and the D grades behind capability dismissal, both preceded by risk feedback that went unanswered.
hypothesis: F1 answers risk feedback by its strength, not its presence. In its 4 Haiku digests it took Defuse legacy risk after 11 of 22 risk-mentioning remarks (5 of 9 at 'piled up' or worse) and in none of the 6 Energy phases after its 3 blow-ups. 3 of the 4 games had a blow-up, one short of a trust crisis, which is how both of F1's Opus losses ended. Across the 86 Haiku digests, taking Defuse in the phase after a mild risk remark cut the rate of blow-ups within three months from 10% (9/93) to 2% (2/110); after a stronger remark it cut it from 20% (10/51) to 8% (13/154). After a calm remark it changed nothing (4% against 4%). The remark was calm again by the month's end in 86% of phases with Defuse against 34% without. Every D grade (37 of 37) came with a risk-mentioning remark in the review month. The new rule treats any non-reassuring risk feedback, or a blow-up since the last phase, as a signal that puts Defuse legacy risk right after Act recovery. It should cut blow-ups, risk-loaded reviews and D grades, and through them trust-crisis and dismissal exits, at a small cost in Prepare report materials.
change: The f1-core-v1 text plus one rule. A 'Risk signal' class: since the last Energy phase, buried problems blew up, or the latest feedback about risk is anything but reassuring. Energy step 2: 'Risk signal next: Defuse legacy risk, however mild the wording'. This replaces F1's step 'After a warning about accumulated or legacy risk, include Defuse legacy risk' and moves it ahead of lifting the weakest. The note example adds 'risk signal' and the description names the rule. Nothing else differs from f1-core-v1, so f1-core-v1 against this policy isolates the trigger; against F1 it also carries the subtraction. 315 words against 486.
predicted_behaviour: Against F1 in the same 4-run Haiku screen: Defuse legacy risk in at least 80% of Energy phases whose latest risk remark was not reassuring (parent 50%, 11 of 22) and in the next Energy phase after any blow-up (parent 0 of 3). Defuse in about half or more of all phases (parent 42%), with Prepare report materials a little below the parent's 73%. Fewer months with a 'piled up'-or-worse remark (parent 11%), fewer reviews held under a risk-mentioning remark, no D grade, fewer blow-ups than the parent's 3 in 4 games and no run with two (no trust crisis). Promotion timing like the parent's (review 1 in at least 3 of 4 runs). Notes cite 'risk signal'. At least 3 of 4 runs complete.
refutation: Refuted as a mechanism if, with the manipulation executed (Defuse after at least 80% of risk signals), risk-mentioning remarks at reviews, D grades and blow-ups are not fewer than the parent's. Refuted as a policy if completion or mean quantitative_score is below both F1's and f1-core-v1's in the same block: the Energy spent on Defuse cost more Output than the risk it removed. The manipulation fails if the response rate stays near the parent's 50%: the actor still reads strength, not presence, and the trigger wording is at fault rather than the hypothesis.
alternative_diagnoses: Blow-ups come mostly from story choices that add hidden risk, so Defuse after the remark is too late and only the story filter matters (then blow-ups do not fall although the response rate rises).
The remark-review link is reverse causal: weak half-years produce both risk remarks and weak grades, so calmer remarks will not lift grades (then remarks at reviews fall but grades do not).
Defuse after a calm remark, which this rule neither asks for nor forbids, is what helped pre-review grades in the F3 family; the rule leaves that untested.
notes: Block 5 (decision #142), F1 child 2 of 2: middle rung of the nested ladder f1-core-v1, f1-risk-signal-v1, f1-status-line-v1. Differs from f1-review-risk-v1 (53.1) in having no REVIEW mode, no main-action switch to Report results or Showcase results, no mode labels, no story-option ban and no exit rule. It changes only what counts as a risk signal and where Defuse sits in the Energy order. F3-lean's Raised state uses a similar trigger; here F1's balance stays and there is no Escalating mode, Lay-low response or weak-review plan. The trigger is pure feedback state (the latest remark, or a blow-up since the last phase); no review cadence, months, numbers or quoted game text.
